newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Silvermines says confident about the future.
newsitem.headline: Silvermines says confident about the future.

text.p: Engineering and technology firm Silvermines Group said on Wednesday that with many opportunities for organic growth across all divisions, including the Joint Venture recently announced with Echlin Inc., it was confident about its future prospects.

"1996 was a year of continued progress for the group during which a number of strategic developments have strengthened the group and created the opportunity for future organic growth," Silvermines Chairman, Bob Morton, said in a results statement.

"The joint venture announced earlier this week with Echlin Inc. for our Automotive Motion Technology Division is a very exciting development. The joint venture partners will share the investment and rewards of this growth market: a major step forward in the evolution of the electric car," he added.
Earlier Silvermines said its pre-tax profit had risen by 18 percent to 4.1 million Irish pounds while turnover had increased by 21 percent to 65 million punts.
Gearing at the year end amounted to 18 percent, it said.
The company said its business activities had been reviewed and restructured with effect from January 1, 1997, into five divisions.

Silvermines said its aerospace division comprising Muirhead Vactric Components Limited and Norcroft Dynamics Limited was strengthened during 1996 by the acquisition in April of Pickering Controls Inc. in the United States.
It said since the acquisition the integration of the two companies had progressed satisfactorily and the benefits were anticipated to contribute to its 1997 results.

The company said the core activities of the division continued to build on the excellent progress made in the two prior years with growth in all of its major markets, aerospace, defence and industrial.

Silvermines said following two years of very high growth in its CCTV and Building Automation Division, 1996 was by contrast a year of consolidation in which it invested heavily in global marketing, new product development and value engineering to consolidate its position as one of the foremost CCTV groups in the world well into the 21st century.

It said all of the companies in this division were growing their businesses in the United States, China and countries in the Pacific Rim, where important major reference installations had been secured in China, Hong Kong, Korea and Thailand.
The new distribution company Molynx BV set up in Holland had made an excellent start in its first year of trading, it said.

Silvermines said trading in its electrical division had improved considerably over the prior year as a result of the best ever order intake in 1995 together with continued good order intake in 1996 including a major contracts from Qatar for 6.5 million Irish pounds.
It said Elequip Projects continued to expand its customer base for the supply of electrical control systems for railway rolling stock.

Silvermines said the Continental Microwave Group, acquired in November 1996 for 10.3 million punts, had been completely integrated within the group and the results since the acquisition had been encouraging with new orders for 1997 in line with our expectations for the year.
It said during the year Marine House and Shannon Business Park were sold for 4.4 million Irish pounds and 2.6 million punts respectively net of expenses.
Both disposals were in accordance with the group's previously stated intention to dispose of all investment property and focus its activities within the electrical and electronics sector, it said.
